title: Screening Canine Feces for Salmonella Species with V-CLASP Culture Method
author: Sarah Nemser
materials: Use pure cultures for biochemical and serological confirmation.
Use the antisera according to the producer's instructions.
Use the antisera according to the producer's instructions.

steps.title: Prepare Initial Fecal Dilution
steps.instruction: Aseptically weigh 10 g of fecal sample into a Whirl-Pak bag and add 90 mL of ambient temperature buffered peptone water (BPW) to achieve a 1/10 dilution.

substeps.instruction: Use a tongue depressor for weighing the sample.
Mix the fecal sample in the bag.

steps.title: Perform Selective Enrichment
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.1 mL of the enriched BPW sample into a tube containing 10 mL of Rappaport-Vassiliadis (RV) broth.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated RV broth at 41.5 °C ± 1 °C for 24 h ± 3 h.
Ensure the maximum incubation temperature does not exceed 42.5 °C.

steps.title: Plate onto Selective Media
steps.instruction: Inoculate XLT4 agar and Brilliant Green with Novobiocin (BGN) agar standard-sized Petri dishes using the enriched RV broth.

substeps.instruction: Take a 10 µL loop of the enriched RV broth.
Spread the loop on the surface of the XLT4 and BGN agar plates to obtain well-isolated colonies.
Invert the dishes (bottom uppermost) and place them in an incubator set at 37 °C.

steps.title: Screen for Typical Salmonella Colonies
steps.instruction: After incubation for 24 h ± 3 h, examine plates for typical Salmonella colonies and mark their positions on the bottom of the dish.

substeps.instruction: Identify XLT4 colonies: black center with a lightly transparent reddish zone.
Identify BGN colonies: pink color.

steps.title: Subculture Presumptive Colonies
steps.instruction: Select at least five typical or suspect colonies from each selective medium dish (or all if fewer than five are present) and streak them onto MacConkey agar plates.

substeps.instruction: Streak in a manner that allows well-isolated colonies to develop.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C ± 1 °C for 24 h ± 3 h.

steps.title: Perform Biochemical Confirmation
steps.instruction: Inoculate Triple Sugar/Iron agar (TSI) and Lysine Iron agar (LIA) with the selected cultures.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate TSI slant by streaking the slant and stabbing the butt using an inoculation needle; incubate at 37 °C ± 1 °C for 18 h ± 2 h (Typical: red slant, yellow butt with gas and H2S blackening).
Inoculate LIA slant by stabbing the butt twice and then streaking the slant; incubate at 37 °C ± 1 °C for 24 h ± 3 h (Typical: alkaline slant and butt with H2S production).

steps.title: Perform Serological and Mass Spectrometry Identification
steps.instruction: Confirm Salmonella identity using agglutination and/or MALDI-TOF MS.

substeps.instruction: Test for Salmonella O-antigens via slide agglutination with polyvalent anti-O sera using pure colonies from TSI/LIA slants or other appropriate media.
Alternatively, sub-culture suspect colonies to blood agar plates, incubate at 37 °C ± 1 °C for 24 ± 3 h, and identify using MALDI-TOF MS according to the manufacturer's protocol.

steps.title: Prepare Isolates for Long-term Storage
steps.instruction: Preserve confirmed isolates in a stabilizing fluid and store at < -70 °C.

substeps.instruction: Incubate organisms overnight on a blood agar plate at 37 °C ± 1 °C for 24 ± 3 h.
Observe colonies for purity and identity (optionally perform a gram stain).

Suspend a very heavy inoculum of colonies in a stabilizing fluid (e.g., sterile 10%-20% glycerol in Brucella broth, defibrinated whole sheep blood, 50% calf serum, or commercial cryopreservation tubes) to make a turbid suspension.
Label two or more freezer vials with isolate number and date on the side, and isolate number on the top.
Place vials in a refrigerator (4 °C) for approximately 30 minutes for quick freezing.
Transfer vials to a freezer box and store at < -70 °C.
